answer: Sybil operators spin fresh keys because admission is cheap. Each applicant books one berth on a public terrace for a 14-minute watch and drives a 9-kg magnetic anchor 2.4 m into silt only when a 7-bit nebula nonce matches the berth mask. Cost is 74 locked units plus berth time. Peers recompute H(pubkey||berth_id||nonce||depth) and drop any berth whose core serial or refund path already sits on another live watch. A missed window or depth outside 2.28-2.52 m burns 18 units and cools the key for six epochs; a reused berth-id or a second miss empties the lock and bars the key for twelve epochs.
